title: Generation of sufficiently divisible Veronese rings
statement: Let k and R be commutative rings, R a k-algebra, and R = direct sum of R_n for n >= 0 a grading by k-submodules. Suppose R is finitely generated as an R_0-algebra. Then there is a positive D such that, for every positive multiple d of D and every n, every element of R_(nd) belongs to the subring generated by R_0 and R_d. Thus sufficiently divisible Veronese rings are generated in degree one over degree zero.

proof.text: Use Mathlib GradedAlgebra.exists_finset_adjoin_eq_top_and_homogeneous_ne_zero to choose finitely many homogeneous positive-degree generators. Pad the list with zero in degree one, so its cardinal r is positive even for a degree-zero ring.

Let l be the product of the positive generator degrees and D=r*l. For d=D*c write d=r*m with m=l*c. If a monomial has degree at least r*m, some exponent is at least m/a_i: otherwise the sum of the weighted exponents is strictly below r*m. Extract a pure-power factor of degree m.

For a monomial of degree n*d with n >= 2, repeat r times and obtain a submonomial of degree d. The remaining degree is (n-1)*d. Induction factors every monomial into degree-d monomials; n=0 is a coefficient in R_0.

The algebra is the R_0-span of monomials in the homogeneous generators. Apply the homogeneous direct-sum projection to retain only monomials of the desired degree; each such monomial belongs to the indicated subring, which is stable under R_0-coefficients and sums.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_veronese_generators [Algebra.FiniteType (𝒜 0) R] :
    ∃ D : ℕ+, ∀ d : ℕ+, (D : ℕ) ∣ (d : ℕ) →
      ∀ (n : ℕ) (a : R), a ∈ 𝒜 (n * (d : ℕ)) →
        a ∈ Subring.closure ((𝒜 0 : Set R) ∪ (𝒜 (d : ℕ) : Set R))
lean.note: Section variables are the commutative rings k,R, Algebra k R, grading 𝒜 and GradedRing 𝒜; VeroneseProjIso also has d : ℕ+.
